sentences.text: The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner is an accused along with two other accused persons in Special Sessions Case (POCSO) No. 98 of 2022 and facing trial of the offence of Section 363, 376(D), 450, 313, 294, 506, 323, 34 of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act.
In the case, the prosecutrix has been examined as PW-1 on 10.03.2023
On the same day, she was being cross-examined by the accused persons.

On 03.04.2024, an application under Section 311 of CrPC Jeetan Sonpakar @ Ladhu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34930598/
1 has been filed by the petitioner/accused before the Learned Trial Court for recalling of the prosecutrix (PW-1) for her re-cross- examination on the ground that after perusal of the evidence of the prosecutrix, it appears that she was not being properly cross- examined by the defence and therefore, she is required to be re- cross-examined.

sentences.text: 3. The application filed by the petitioner/accused was decided by the Learned Trial Court on 28.08.2024 and has dismissed the application by holding that the prosecutrix has been detailed cross-examined by the defence on 10.03.2023 and after about 1 year and 5 months of her examination, the present application has been filed, which is highly belated and has dismissed the application, which is under challenge in the present petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that on 10.03.2023 when the prosecutrix has been examined as PW-1, some important questions were missed in cross-examination and certain omissions and contradictions in her evidence is also left for its confrontation, which materially affects the defence of the accused for which re- cross-examination of the prosecutrix is necessary.
He would also submit that the mistake of the counsel to put proper question in cross-examination, the accused cannot be punished.
He would also submit that the mother of the prosecutrix has sworn an affidavit with the effect that she has no objection, if the accused is being discharged from the case.
Therefore, the prosecutrix (PW-1) may be recalled for her re-cross-examination by the defence.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes and has submitted that the prosecutrix was detailed cross-examined on 10.03.2023 on each and every aspect of the matter and it is only when the mother of the prosecutrix sworn an affidavit that she has no objection in the case, if the accused is being discharged from the case.
The defence is trying to bring the said affidavit on record by way of re-cross-examination of the prosecutrix.

He would also submit that after completion of the examination and cross-examination of the prosecutrix that too after long lapse of time, when the other witnesses have also been examined, she cannot be recalled for further re-cross-examination to fulfill the lacuna, whereas, in the present case, the defence is trying to tamper with the witness and bring the said affidavit on record by way of re-cross-examination of the prosecutrix, which is not permissible.
Therefore, the Learned Trial Court has rightly dismissed the application filed by the petitioner and there is no ground for interference in the impugned order.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents annexed with the petition.

7. From the document (Annexure P-1), which is the deposition of the prosecutrix (PW-1), it appears that the prosecutrix was detailed cross-examined by the counsel of the accused, which is recorded on 10.03.2023.
The evidence of the prosecutrix was recorded in presence of the mother of the prosecutrix.
The prosecutrix (PW-1) was detailed cross-examined including the questions put by the Learned Trial Court and further re-cross-examined by the defence

. In the application filed by the petitioner/accused (Annexure P-2) before the Learned Trial Court under Section 311 of CrPC, the grounds for recalling of the prosecutrix for her re-cross-examination is mentioned that the prosecutrix was not properly cross-examined by the defence and therefore she may be recalled for further re-cross-examination.
The grounds taken by the defence in the application is very vague.

2 application under Section 311 of CrPC is filed on 03.04.2024, whereas the examination and cross-examination of the prosecutrix has been completed on 10.03.2023.

sentences.text: Thus, the application has been filed after about more than one year, which appears to be highly belated and from the document (Annexure P-4), which is an affidavit executed by the mother of the prosecutrix, it also appears that the defence wants to bring the said affidavit on record by way of re- cross-examination of the prosecutrix (PW-1).

Once the examination and cross-examination of the prosecutrix has been completed and she duly supported the prosecution's case, in the subsequent and belated stage that too on vague grounds, she cannot be recalled for her re-cross-examination, except for the other compelling reasons, which may prejudice the defence of the accused.
The prosecutrix cannot be recalled for her re-cross-examination to fulfill the lacuna or to bring the subsequent affidavit on record executed by her mother.

sentences.text: That brings us to the next question as to whether the High Court was justified in setting aside the order of the Sessions Judge and allowing the application filed by PWs 4 and 5 for their re-examination.
For ready reference Section 311 of the Cr.P.C.

is as under:
"311. Power to summon material witness, or examine person present.-

Any Court may, at any stage of any inquiry, trial or other proceeding under this Code, summon any person as a witness, or examine any person in attendance, though not summoned as a witness, or recall and re-examine any person already examined; and the Court shall summon and examine or recall and re-examine any such person if his evidence appears to it to be essential to the just decision of the case".

17. In order to enable the court to find out the truth and render a just decision, the salutary provisions of Section 311 are enacted whereunder any court by exercising its discretionary authority at any stage of inquiry, trial or other proceeding can summon any person as witness or examine any person in attendance though not summoned as a witness or recall or re-examine any person already examined who are expected to be able to throw light upon the matter in dispute.
The object of the provision as a whole is to do justice not only from the point of view of the accused and the prosecution but also from the point of view of an orderly society.
This power is to be exercised only for strong and valid reasons and it should be exercised with caution and circumspection.
Recall is not a matter of course and the discretion given to the court has to be exercised judicially to prevent failure of justice.
Therefore, the reasons for exercising this power should be spelt out in the order.

18. In Vijay Kumar v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr., (2011) 8 SCC 136, this Court while explaining scope and ambit of Section 311 has held as under:-
"17.

entities.text: Vijay Kumar v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr., (2011) 8 SCC 136
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though Section 311 confers vast discretion upon the court and is expressed in the widest possible terms, the discretionary power under the said section can be invoked only for the ends of justice.

Discretionary power should be exercised consistently with Jeetan Sonpakar @ Ladhu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34930598/
3 the provisions of CrPC and the principles of criminal law.

entities.text: Jeetan Sonpakar @ Ladhu vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The discretionary power conferred under Section 311 has to be exercised judicially for reasons stated by the court and not arbitrarily or capriciously".

19. In Zahira Habibullah Sheikh (5) and Anr. v. State of Gujarat and Others, (2006) 3 SCC 374, this Court has considered the concept underlining under Section 311 as under:-
"27.

entities.text: Zahira Habibullah Sheikh (5) and Anr. v. State of Gujarat and Others, (2006) 3 SCC 374
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The object underlying Section 311 of the Code is that there may not be failure of justice on account of mistake of either party in bringing the valuable evidence on record or leaving ambiguity in the statements of the witnesses examined from either side.
The determinative factor is whether it is essential to the just decision of the case.

The section is not limited only for the benefit of the accused, and it will not be an improper exercise of the powers of the court to summon a witness under the section merely because the evidence supports the case of the prosecution and not that of the accused.

The section is a general section which applies to all proceedings, enquiries and trials under the Code and empowers the Magistrate to issue summons to any witness at any stage of such proceedings, trial or enquiry.
In Section 311 the significant expression that occurs is "at any stage of any inquiry or trial or other proceeding under this Code".

It is, however, to be borne in mind that whereas the section confers a very wide power on the court on summoning witnesses, the discretion conferred is to be exercised judiciously, as the wider the power the greater is the necessity for application of judicial mind".
20.

In State (NCT of Delhi) v. Shiv Kumar Yadav & Anr., (2016) 2 SCC 402, it was held thus:-
"............... Certainly, recall could be permitted if essential for the just decision, but not on such consideration as has been adopted in the present case.

entities.text: State (NCT of Delhi) v. Shiv Kumar Yadav & Anr., (2016) 2 SCC 402
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mere observation that recall was necessary "for ensuring fair trial" is not enough unless there are tangible reasons to show how the fair trial suffered without recall.
Recall is not a matter of course and the discretion given to the court has to be exercised judiciously to prevent failure of justice and not arbitrarily.

While the party is even permitted to correct its bona fide error and may be entitled to further opportunity even when such opportunity may be sought without any fault on the part of the opposite party, plea for recall for advancing justice has to be bona fide and has to be balanced carefully with the other relevant considerations including uncalled for hardship to the witnesses and uncalled for delay in the trial.

Having regard to these considerations,
there is no ground to justify the recall of witnesses already examined".
21.
The delay in filing the application is one of the important factors which has to explained in the application.

sentences.text: Before parting, however, we may notice that a contention has been raised by the learned counsel for the appellant that PW 1 who was examined in Court on 5-7- 1994 purported to have filed an application on 1-5-1995 stating that five accused persons named therein were innocent.
An application filed by him purported to be under Section 311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was rejected by the learned trial Judge by order dated 13-5-1995.
A revision petition was filed thereagainst and the High Court also rejected the said contention.
It is not a case where stricto sensu the provisions of Section 311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure could have been invoked.
The very fact that such an application was got filed by PW 1 nine months after his deposition is itself pointer to the fact that he had been won over.
It is absurd to contend that he, after a period of four years and that too after his examination-in-chief and cross- examination was complete, would file an application on his own will and volition.
The said application was, therefore, rightly dismissed".
22. Coming to the facts of the present case, PWs 4 and 5 were examined between 29.11.2010 and 11.3.2011.
They were cross-examined at length during the said period.
During the police investigation and in their evidence, they have supported the prosecution story.
The Sessions Judge has recorded a finding that they were not under any pressure while recording their evidence.
After a passage of 14 months, they have filed the application for their re- examination on the ground that the statements made by them earlier were under pressure.
They have not assigned any reasons for the delay in making application.
It is obvious that they had been won over.
We do not find any reasons to allow such an application.

The Sessions Judge, therefore,
was justified in rejecting the application.
In our view, High Court was not right in setting aside the said order.

"
9. A perusal of the impugned order makes it clear that the prosecutrix was examined and cross-examined fully long back.

A lengthy cross- examination was put to prosecutrix and she gave reply all the questions put to her,
but later on, an affidavit was filed in the present petition by her mother, wherein the mother of the prosecutrix has stated that she and her daughter have no objection if the accused is being discharged from the offence.
The affidavit is contrary to the evidence of the prosecutrix (PW-1) and she fully supported the prosecution case.
After a passage of time, the accused has filed an application for re-cross-examination on the ground that some of the questions are yet to be put before her.
No reason has been assigned for the delay in moving application.
The entire scenario shows that she has been one over by the defence.
It is the settled of law that the benefit of Section 311 of CrPC cannot be extended to the accused to fill up the lacuna.

Mere submissions that some questions could not be put to the prosecutrix in her lengthy cross-examination, cannot be a ground to recall her, who has already been examined and cross- Jeetan Sonpakar @ Ladhu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34930598/
5 examined at length.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The provisions of Section 311 of CrPC can be invoked only in order to meet the ends of justice for strong and valid reasons, with great caution and circumspection and not to permit the accused to call the prosecutrix again and again for re-cross- examination.

In Manghi @ Narendra v. State of M.P., (2005) 4 MPLJ 136, the Madhya Pradesh High Court has held that "once the witness is examined as a prosecution witness, he cannot be recalled for examination/cross-examination,
merely because he filed affidavit contrary to his deposition made before the Trial Court".

entities.text: Manghi @ Narendra v. State of M.P., (2005) 4 MPLJ 136
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Unfair advantage cannot be given to any of the parties and no one can be permitted to recall the witness for further re-cross-examination, merely on the ground that an affidavit has been filed by the defence after her deposition before the Trial Court.
10. In view of the above discussions, this Court does not find any error in the impugned order and is not inclined to interfere with it.
Accordingly, the petition, being sans merits, is hereby dismissed.
